# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42 (Bi-Vb Pc42)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc42
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42
**Title (English, from literature):** Using luxurious furniture

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āsandiparibhuñjana Sikkhāpada* ("Using luxurious furniture", Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42) is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Theravāda tradition [Catalog]. The rule establishes that a nun who uses a large, high, or luxurious seat or couch (such as an *āsandi*, a deckchair or divan) commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravādin Vinaya regulations for nuns, Ute Hüsken notes that like monks, nuns are prohibited from using certain furniture items such as easy chairs or divans (*Pāc 42*) as part of general restrictions on worldly luxuries and improper personal requisites [Hüsken 1997].

 Modern English translations of the rule include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
